Experienced Mechanical Supervisor required for a mining construction project. 8/6 roster, camp provided, FIFO    Your new company    Our client is a leading resources organisation delivering large-scale projects across Queensland's mining sector. With a strong focus on safety, operational excellence, and project delivery, they offer the opportunity to work on significant construction works while contributing to the ongoing growth and success of a major mining operation. 
   Your new role    As the Mechanical Supervisor, you will be responsible for overseeing mechanical construction activities and ensuring all work is completed safely, efficiently, and in line with project and site requirements. 
 Key responsibilities will include: 
 
 Supervising mechanical construction works across the project 
 Ensuring all activities comply with the Queensland Coal Mining Safety and Health Management System (SHMS) 
 Coordinating contractors, trades, and site personnel 
 Managing daily work scopes and construction schedules 
 Monitoring work quality and ensuring compliance with project specifications 
 Conducting safety inspections, toolbox talks, and risk assessments 
 Providing leadership, mentoring, and technical support to mechanical teams 
 Identifying and mitigating project risks and construction issues 
 Reporting on project progress, resources, and field activities 
 
   What you'll need to succeed  
 
 
 Demonstrated experience supervising construction works within a Queensland coal mining SHMS environment 
 
 Strong experience in mechanical construction methodologies 
 Proven ability to lead and manage multidisciplinary work crews 
 Excellent communication and stakeholder management skills 
 Strong commitment to safety leadership and compliance 
 Ability to coordinate contractors and manage competing priorities 
 Relevant mechanical trade qualification or engineering qualification 
 Current Australian driving licence 
 
   What you'll get in return  
 This is an excellent opportunity to secure a role on a significant mining construction project with a reputable industry leader. You'll work alongside experienced professionals in a collaborative environment where safety and project success are key priorities. The role offers an attractive Wednesday-to-Wednesday 8/6 roster, camp accommodation, and the flexibility of FIFO or DIDO arrangements, providing a strong work-life balance while working on a high-profile project.

Location: Arana Hills, QLD, 4054
Full-Time: Immediate start
Reports to: Centre Manager & ECT
Job Title: Early Childhood Teacher
Salary range: $80,000 - $90,000 + Superannuation
Job Closure date: 30 days

About This Role:
On behalf of our client, we are pleased to introduce a warm and nurturing early learning centre located in Arana Hills. The centre is dedicated to fostering a lifelong love of learning through a supportive, play-based environment where every child is encouraged to explore, grow, and develop confidence.
Operating as a close-knit community, the centre accommodates children from 6 weeks to 5 years old. It is committed to the highest standards, consistently meeting the National Quality Standard to deliver exceptional care and education

Key Duties & Responsibilities:
Curriculum & Pedagogy:
• Design, implement, and evaluate a comprehensive educational program aligned with the Early Years Learning Framework (EYLF) and the service's philosophy.
• Employ intentional teaching strategies within a play-based learning environment to foster cognitive, social, and emotional development.
• Lead engaging learning experiences across key domains, including literacy, numeracy, creative arts, and physical activity.

Assessment & Documentation:
• Conduct detailed observations and use critical reflection to assess children's learning and progress against individual and group goals.
• Create rich and detailed portfolios and learning stories that make children's learning visible to families and colleagues.
• Use documented evidence to plan forward and ensure a dynamic, responsive curriculum.

Leadership & Mentorship:
• Provide guidance and support to other educators within the room, modelling best practices in early childhood teaching.
• Contribute to a collaborative culture of continuous improvement and reflective practice among the teaching team.

Family & Community Partnership:
• Build strong, respectful, and collaborative partnerships with families through formal and informal communication.
• Lead family-teacher meetings and discussions about child development and learning goals.
• Actively participate in community events and centre initiatives to strengthen community ties.

Compliance & Professionalism:
• Ensure all practices meet the National Quality Standard and relevant regulatory requirements.
• Maintain a safe, inclusive, and stimulating learning environment for all children.
• Engage in ongoing professional development and contribute to the service's quality improvement plan.

Skills & Requirements:
• A Bachelor of Early Childhood Education (or ACECQA-approved equivalent) is essential.
• A current and valid Victorian Institute of Teaching (VIT) Registration.
• Proven experience as an Early Childhood Teacher within a long day care or similar setting.
• Deep knowledge and practical application of the Early Years Learning Framework (EYLF) and National Quality Standards (NQS).
• Exceptional communication and interpersonal skills for building relationships with children, families, and colleagues.
• Current First Aid, Asthma & Anaphylaxis Certification (HLTAID012).
• A valid Working with Children Check and National Police Check.
• Proof of up-to-date vaccination status as per service policy.

Why Apply?
This is more than a job - it's an opportunity to shape young lives in an environment that values educator wellbeing as much as child development. You'll receive:

• Above-award wages for qualified candidates
• Paid professional development opportunities
• Supportive leadership team with realistic expectations
• Purpose-built facilities with quality resources

If you're ready to make your mark in early childhood education with an organisation that values your expertise, we'd love to hear from you.

How to Apply:
Submit your resume and cover letter addressing your experience with the EYLF and your approach to play-based learning. Successful applicants will require valid working rights and must pass background checks.

Please note: We are acting as recruitment agents on behalf of our client. Employer details will be provided to shortlisted candidates.

MedicalJobsAustralia.com     Your Position at St John of God Bendigo Hospital

We are seeking applications from suitably qualified Nurse Unit Managers (NUMs) to join our highly skilled Oncology Department on a permanent full-time basis. This is an exciting opportunity to lead a dedicated multidisciplinary team delivering comprehensive cancer care services across our Day Oncology unit. Working within a supportive and collaborative environment, you will play a key role in shaping the future of the service while ensuring exceptional outcomes for patients and their families.

As the Nurse Unit Manager, you will be responsible for the overall management of the department, including workforce planning, financial and resource management, quality and risk oversight, and the implementation of strategic and operational initiatives. You will ensure the department meets key performance indicators and maintains compliance with National and State standards, accreditation requirements, and regulatory obligations, while contributing to the Hospital's strategic objectives and fostering a culture of continuous improvement and professional development.

The Position

Monitor standards of service and practice against benchmark targets, including nurse sensitive indicators, incident management system data, clinical indicator results and patient, doctor and caregiver satisfaction results. Where benchmarks are not met, design, implement and evaluate responses.

Support and participate in the ACHS accreditation process-regulatory assessments, as well as group-wide and divisional Quality and Clinical Risk Management programs.

Foster a clinical culture of interdisciplinary collaboration to improve patient outcomes. Ensure that patients and consumers are actively involved in relevant planning and decision-making processes.

Works in a clinical capacity within the department as required, to support caregivers, medical officers and to ensure the delivery of safe, person centred care.

Ongoing financial management and monitoring of the service cost centre including, productivity, activity and utilisation in line with budgetary parameters and performance targets.

Promotes and demonstrates a culture of innovation and improvement to enhance patient care and experience. In consultation with Hospital Management Committee, actively contributes to marketing the service to Medical Practitioners

You will be registered with the Nursing and Midwifery Board of Australia as a Registered Nurse and demonstrate advanced clinical skills, strong relationship-building abilities, and relevant oncology nursing knowledge and experience. Postgraduate qualifications in Oncology Nursing, Management, or a related discipline will be highly regarded.

To succeed in this role, you will have contemporary leadership and management experience in a senior nursing position within an acute hospital setting, with the ability to lead teams, drive positive patient outcomes, and support a culture of clinical excellence.

Above all, patients will be at the core of everything you do committing to and supporting our Mission and Values.

The Benefits:

Salary: $147,618 per annum, plus 12% superannuation

A permanent full-time position, working up to 38 hours per fortnight.

Salary packaging up to $18,550 on a range of benefits such as mortgage, rent, meal entertainment, holiday accommodation or other everyday living expenses as well as options to salary package benefits above the FBT cap on items such as:

Novated leasing 

work related expenses

self-education and

additional superannuation

A healthy work-life balance through flexible work options, additional purchased leave and well-being programs

Employee discount on St John of God Hospital & Medical Services and Private Health Insurance

Dynamic multidisciplinary team

For enquiries contact Elizabeth McEncroe, DON on (03) 5434 3231

If suitable applicants are identified advertisement may close prior to listed date

At St John of God Health Care, we celebrate diversity and warmly welcome applications from people of all backgrounds. 

Our commitment is to create a safe and nurturing environment for all children and vulnerable individuals in our care and proactively take steps to protect them from abuse, ensuring their safety and well-being. 

Our inclusive culture fosters an environment that is respectful and secure, welcoming and accessible, and unified through our diverse community.

In this role, you will be responsible for installing, commissioning, testing and maintaining fibre optic telecommunications infrastructure across Telstra and NBN projects. You will perform fibre splicing, network testing, fault diagnosis and commissioning activities between the exchange and customer network boundary, while ensuring compliance with Telstra, NBN and company technical standards.  As part of our growing team, you will play a key role in delivering telecommunications infrastructure projects across New South Wales.(Sydney & Newcastle) You will work closely with project managers, clients and field teams to support network upgrades, customer connections and maintenance activities, while contributing to the successful delivery of high-quality telecommunications solutions.   Duties included are:    Install, commission and maintain fibre optic and telecommunications network infrastructure across Telstra and NBN projects.   Perform fibre handling, cable hauling, splicing, termination, testing and fault diagnosis using OTDR, power meters and other telecommunications testing equipment.   Conduct network fault finding, diagnostics and preventative maintenance to ensure reliable network performance.   Interpret telecommunications network plans, design drawings and technical specifications to complete field installations.   Configure, commission and test fibre optic network components to ensure network performance and service quality.   Manage client sites and coordinate field activities to ensure projects are completed safely, efficiently and in compliance with client requirements.   Prepare technical reports, test results, as-built documentation, installation records and upload project artefacts through client management systems.   Assist with telecommunications network upgrades, commissioning activities and customer network connections.   Assist with minor civil works associated with the installation of telecommunications infrastructure, including conduit preparation, pit and pipe works, cable hauling and site set-up where required.   Ensure all installations and maintenance activities comply with Telstra, NBN and company technical standards, quality requirements and safety procedures.    Skills and experience:    Minimum one year of experience in fibre optic telecommunications, telecommunications network installation, or a related field.   Qualification in Information Technology (Telecommunications Network Engineering) or a related discipline.   Demonstrated experience in fibre handling, splicing, testing and fault diagnosis using telecommunications testing equipment (e.g. OTDR and power meters).   Strong knowledge of Telstra and NBN fibre optic networks, installation standards and commissioning procedures.   Experience interpreting telecommunications network plans, technical drawings and specifications.   Knowledge of telecommunications civil infrastructure, including conduit, pit and pipe installations and cable hauling.   Experience operating plant and equipment, including excavators (desirable).   Strong problem-solving skills with the ability to diagnose and resolve network faults.   Excellent organisational and communication skills, with the ability to manage multiple tasks and client requirements.   Ability to work independently and collaboratively in a team environment.   Willingness to learn, adapt to new technologies and work across a variety of project environments.      WHO ARE WE LOOKING FOR?    The successful candidate will:   Have the ability to work (Monday to Friday)  Be well organised  Have attention to detail  Be self-motivated and willing to learn  Be able to prioritise and manage time  Be able to work with multiple senior level employees and manage upwards and downwards  prior experience required!        About Company     Civil Network Corp is a progressive Fibre & Civil works contractor based in Sydney & Newcastle with ongoing projects right across the state providing design, construction, management, maintenance, and field services solutions for fixed and wireless networks. Driven by our values - delivering results, building strong relationships, and striving for continual progression.         Salary:  $80000-90000   Job Publish:  20-07-2026   Job Expire:  19-08-2026  Apply on:  Telecommunications field engineer Job here! Global Vision Recruitment on behalf of DMC Electrical and Air Cooling Pty Ltd

Date Posted: 10 July 2026

Position: Mechanical Engineer

Salary: $80,000 - $100,000 per annum plus 12% superannuation

Mode: Full-time

Hours: 38 hours per week

Location: 11 Parkside Drive, Condon QLD 4815

Experience required: Minimum 1 year experience as a Mechanical Engineer or in a similar role

DMC Electrical and Air Cooling Pty Ltd is a well-established provider of commercial and residential electrical, air conditioning, HVAC, and sheet metal solutions, proudly servicing Condon and surrounding regions for nearly 40 years. The company specialises in the design, fabrication, installation, maintenance, and repair of mechanical air conditioning and ventilation systems, delivering high-quality solutions tailored to each client's needs. 

Due to continued growth, we are seeking a qualified and motivated Mechanical Engineer to join our team. This role is ideal for an engineer with strong experience in HVAC system design, ductwork engineering, heat load calculations, AutoCAD drafting, and project management.

Key Responsibilities include but not limited to:

•	Design HVAC and ventilation systems for commercial and residential projects, ensuring efficient, practical, and compliant mechanical solutions. 

•	Perform heat load calculations and airflow analysis to determine equipment capacities and optimise system performance. 

•	Prepare detailed 2D AutoCAD drawings and 3D mechanical models for ductwork layouts, plant rooms, and equipment installations. 

•	Design ducting systems, select suitable mechanical equipment, and prepare technical specifications for fabrication and installation. 

•	Manage multiple mechanical projects from design through to installation and commissioning, ensuring completion within agreed budgets and timeframes. 

•	Prepare engineering documentation including mechanical drawings, material schedules, equipment selections, fabrication details, and project reports. 

•	Estimate material quantities, project costs, labour requirements, and procurement schedules to support successful project delivery. 

•	Conduct site inspections, testing, commissioning, and performance assessments to verify system functionality and identify engineering improvements where required. 

•	Analyse technical data, resolve engineering issues, and recommend practical solutions to improve system efficiency, constructability, and operational performance. 

•	Liaise closely with electrical, refrigeration, sheet metal, and construction teams to ensure seamless coordination across multidisciplinary projects. 

•	Ensure all engineering designs, installations, and completed works comply with relevant Australian Standards, the National Construction Code (NCC), workplace health and safety legislation, and contractual requirements. 

Qualifications:

•	Tertiary qualification in Mechanical Engineering or a related discipline. 

•	Minimum 1 year experience as a Mechanical Engineer or in a similar role. 

Other Skills and Requirements: 

•	Demonstrated experience in HVAC system design, duct design, and heat load calculations. 

•	Proficiency in AutoCAD 2D and experience developing 3D mechanical drawings/models. 

•	Strong project coordination and project management skills within mechanical services or HVAC projects. 

•	Knowledge of Australian Standards, NCC requirements, and mechanical engineering principles relating to air conditioning and ventilation systems. 

•	Excellent analytical, problem-solving, communication, and organisational skills. 

•	Ability to manage multiple projects while maintaining high standards of quality, safety, and attention to detail. 

If you are an experienced Mechanical Engineer seeking a long-term opportunity with a respected and growing mechanical services company, we encourage you to apply and become part of the team at DMC Electrical and Air Cooling Pty Ltd. 

Email your resume to recruit@gvrc.com.au. Please note that only shortlisted candidate will be contacted.

Location:   Queanbeyan (Servicing Canberra & Regional NSW)  
  Travel:   Heavy local regional travel + interstate trips monthly (with overnight stays)  
 
   About the Company  
  Our client is within the fire and safety sector based out of Queanbeyan. Operating in an industry where compliance, responsiveness, and trust are non-negotiable, they provide critical safety solutions to commercial, residential, and tier-1 construction clients. Due to strong market demand and strategic growth plans, they are now seeking a sales focused Business Development Manager to increase their pipeline and drive revenue expansion.   
   About the Role  
  This is a role designed for a commercial sales professional who thrives on the road, building face-to-face relationships and closing high-value contracts. This is a new role for the business and while you will be supported by an internal team, the primary focus is pure business development, identifying new market opportunities, securing formal appointments with key decision-makers, and converting leads into long-term commercial accounts.   
  This role does require travel, split between the local market and travelling interstate to capture wider markets.  
   Key Responsibilities  
  New Business Generation & Pipeline Growth  
 
  Identify, target, and secure new business opportunities across Canberra, and the surrounding capital region.  
  Initiate contact with property managers, tier-1/2 builders, compliance officers, and strata managers to secure formal presentations and tender opportunities.  
  Conduct thorough assessments to understand client compliance needs, delivering tailored fire and safety solutions.  
  Lead the preparation and submission of comprehensive commercial proposals, ensuring alignment with client requirements and company profit margins.  
 
  Territory & Market Expansion  
 
  Actively manage your schedule to maintain a high-visibility presence on the ground across the region.  
  Undertake interstate overnight trips to pitch to national accounts, secure large-scale contracts, and establish new regional footprints.  
  Stay ahead of building code changes, industry regulations, and competitor movements to position our client as the preferred provider.  
 
  Strategic Sales Leadership  
 
  Work closely with the internal sales team to align lead generation with overall company revenue objectives.  
  Review the active sales pipeline weekly to identify any friction points in the sales cycle - step in to assist with closing complex deals, and ensure momentum is maintained.  
  Maintain meticulous records of client interactions, upcoming opportunities, and forecasting metrics within the CRM to guide strategic decision-making.  
 
   What You Bring  
 
  Minimum 2 years of experience in a Business Development or a consultative Sales role, ideally within construction, building materials, trade services, or the fire/safety sector.  
  A proven track record of successfully opening doors, cold-calling, and converting cold prospects into loyal clients.  
  Outstanding communication and negotiation skills, with the ability to build immediate rapport with both site managers and corporate executives.  
  Highly self-motivated, disciplined with time management, and comfortable working autonomously while frequently on the road.  
  A valid Australian driver's license is essential, along with a genuine willingness to undertake heavy local driving and required interstate overnight trips.  
  A solid understanding of workplace health and safety (WHS) and building compliance standards is highly regarded.  
 
 
  To Apply  
  If you are a driven sales professional ready to take ownership of a lucrative territory and drive substantial business growth, we want to hear from you.  

 At Randstad, we are passionate about providing equal employment opportunities and embracing diversity to the benefit of all. We actively encourage applications from any background. 
   
    Please  click here  to apply.

Location	Annerley, QLD, 4103
Full-Time	Immediate start
Reports to:	Centre Manager & ECT
Job Title	Early Childhood Teacher
Salary Range	$80,000 - $90,000 + Superannuation - depending on skill level.
Job Closes Date	30 Days  

About the Role
We are partnering with a highly respected early learning provider to find a nurturing and dedicated Early Childhood Teacher for their vibrant centre. This organisation is known for its commitment to nurturing children's growth through a play-based and holistic curriculum. With purpose-built facilities and a team of passionate educators, they create warm, inclusive environments where children feel safe, valued, and inspired to explore and learn.

Key Responsibilities
Curriculum & Pedagogy:
• Design, implement, and evaluate a comprehensive educational program aligned with the Early Years Learning Framework (EYLF) and the service's philosophy.
• Employ intentional teaching strategies within a play-based learning environment to foster cognitive, social, and emotional development.
• Lead engaging learning experiences across key domains, including literacy, numeracy, creative arts, and physical activity.

Assessment & Documentation:
• Conduct detailed observations and use critical reflection to assess children's learning and progress against individual and group goals.
• Create rich and detailed portfolios and learning stories that make children's learning visible to families and colleagues.
• Use documented evidence to plan forward and ensure a dynamic, responsive curriculum.

Leadership & Mentorship:
• Provide guidance and support to other educators within the room, modelling best practices in early childhood teaching.
• Contribute to a collaborative culture of continuous improvement and reflective practice among the teaching team.

Family & Community Partnership:
• Build strong, respectful, and collaborative partnerships with families through formal and informal communication.
• Lead family-teacher meetings and discussions about child development and learning goals.
• Actively participate in community events and centre initiatives to strengthen community ties.

Compliance & Professionalism:
• Ensure all practices meet the National Quality Standard and relevant regulatory requirements.
• Maintain a safe, inclusive, and stimulating learning environment for all children.
• Engage in ongoing professional development and contribute to the service's quality improvement plan.

Skills & Experience
• A Bachelor of Early Childhood Education (or ACECQA-approved equivalent) is essential.
• A current and valid Victorian Institute of Teaching (VIT) Registration.
• Proven experience as an Early Childhood Teacher within a long day care or similar setting.
• Deep knowledge and practical application of the Early Years Learning Framework (EYLF) and National Quality Standards (NQS).
• Exceptional communication and interpersonal skills for building relationships with children, families, and colleagues.
• Current First Aid, Asthma & Anaphylaxis Certification (HLTAID012).
• A valid Working with Children Check and National Police Check.
• Proof of up-to-date vaccination status as per service policy.

Why Apply?
This is more than a job - it's an opportunity to shape young lives in an environment that values educator wellbeing as much as child development. You'll receive:
• Above-award wages for qualified candidates
• Paid professional development opportunities
• Supportive leadership team with realistic expectations
• Purpose-built facilities with quality resources

If you're ready to make your mark in early childhood education with an organisation that values your expertise, we'd love to hear from you.

How to Apply:
Submit your resume and cover letter addressing your experience with the EYLF and your approach to play-based learning. Successful applicants will require valid working rights and must pass background checks.

Please note: We are acting as recruitment agents on behalf of our client. Employer details will be provided to shortlisted candidates.
